messages.subject: How can I get the output with z- and p- vlaue of variances from latent growth curve analyses?
parts:
Dear Lavaan users,

I`m trying to set up a simple latent growth curve model with three time points consisting of two latent
variables (i.e. an intercept and a slope). I'd like to get estimates of variance and intercepts (means) of
the two variables with z- and p- values. While I can find intercept estimates of latent variables with z-
and p- values from summary output, however, z- and p- values don't accompany variance estimates
of the two latent variables when printing summary output as can be seen as follows. 


                   Estimate  Std.err  Z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all
Latent variables:
  i =~
    Y1.kor            1.000                               0.072    0.827
    Y2.kor            1.000                               0.072    0.948
    Y3.kor            1.000                               0.072    1.293
  s =~
    Y1.kor            0.000                               0.000    0.000
    Y2.kor            1.000                               0.023    0.302
    Y3.kor            2.000                               0.046    0.824

Covariances:
  i ~~
    s                -0.001    0.000  -18.634    0.000   -0.750   -0.750

Intercepts:
    Y1.kor            0.000                               0.000    0.000
    Y2.kor            0.000                               0.000    0.000
    Y3.kor            0.000                               0.000    0.000
    i                 2.470    0.001 2435.771    0.000   34.412   34.412
    s                 0.113    0.000  264.055    0.000    4.930    4.930

Variances:
    Y1.kor            0.002    0.000                      0.002    0.316
    Y2.kor            0.003    0.000                      0.003    0.440
    Y3.kor            0.001    0.000                      0.001    0.248
    i                 0.005    0.000       (no value      1.000    1.000
    s                 0.001    0.000       presented)     1.000    1.000

In addition, anybody who knows how to get p-value of the correlation coefficient between the intercept
and the slope? I could find correlation coefficient using "inspect" function, but it showed only the coefficient
without p-value. Thank you users in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How can I get the output with z- and p- vlaue of variances from latent growth curve analyses?
parts: While I can find intercept estimates of latent variables with z- and p- values from summary output, however, z- and p- values don't accompany variance estimates of the two latent variables when printing summary output
You can get them from the output of parameterEstimates()

In addition, anybody who knows how to get p-value of the correlation coefficient between the intercept
and the slope? I could find correlation coefficient using "inspect" function, but it showed only the coefficient
without p-value.

You refer to the p value of the covariance (seen in the summary output) to test the null hypothesis that the covariance (and by implication, the correlation) is zero.  You just look at the "std.all" column to interpret the covariance in a more familiar standardized/correlation metric.  

It may not be worth the extra effort, but if you really want the correlation to be an actual model parameter, you can use phantom variables for the growth factors:
  • regress each growth factor on a phantom variable (regression slopes will be the standard deviations of the growth factors)
  • fix the original growth factor variances (and their covariance) to zero
  • fix the phantom variable variances to one
  • the estimated covariance between the phantom variables will be in correlation metric because the phantom variances = 1.
Terry

messages.subject: Re: How can I get the output with z- and p- vlaue of variances from latent growth curve analyses?
parts:
My R script for a simple latent growth model is as follows:

model.kor <- '#i and s
i =~ 1*Y1.kor + 1*Y2.kor + 1*Y3.kor
s =~ 0*Y1.kor + 1*Y2.kor + 2*Y3.kor'

In addition, if you have enough time to deal with other issues on latent growth modelling, please read my other new post too.
Thank you for your kindness.

Galaxy

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How can I get the output with z- and p- vlaue of variances from latent growth curve analyses?
parts:
1. regress each growth factor on a phantom variable (regression slopes will be the standard deviations of the growth factors)
  2. fix the original growth factor variances (and their covariance) to zero
  3. fix the phantom variable variances to one
  4. the estimated covariance between the phantom variables will be in correlation metric because the phantom variances = 1.

model.kor <- '#i and s
i =~ 1*Y1.kor + 1*Y2.kor + 1*Y3.kor
s =~ 0*Y1.kor + 1*Y2.kor + 2*Y3.kor

#1
ph_i =~ i
ph_s =~ s

#2
i ~~ 0*i + 0*s
s ~~ 0*s

#3
ph_i ~~ 1*ph_i
ph_s ~~ 1*ph_s

#4
ph_i ~~ NA*ph_s
'

The fit of the model will be identical, all you do is change the parametarization (you estimate the growth 2 parameters' SDs rather than variances; everything else you add is just fixed parameters).  This text on longitudinal SEM has more examples and discussion of phantom variables:

http://www.guilford.com/books/Longitudinal-Structural-Equation-Modeling/Todd-Little/9781462510160/reviews

Terry
